solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pirates prohibit song (the way it's sung)

parts.note: to prohibit is to ban

indicators.note: says the song's word is written as it sounds when sung, not as normally spelt

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: Buccaneers outlaw a shanty, with a note on how it should be performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the way it's sung' respells DITTY by its sound as DITTI, giving the old Italian-style plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is an old plural for outlaws or brigands, and pirates are robbers of the sea.

clue.text: Tone adopted when Queen Victoria was depressed

parts.note: the monarch Victoria was a royal
feeling depressed is feeling blue

explanation.surface: A grim note entered the court when the old Queen was in low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tone' looks like a voice or mood, but it means a shade of colour here.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep bright shade, and a tone can mean a particular tint of colour.

clue.text: Radical few recruited by Inland Revenue

indicators.note: being recruited by something means being taken into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: IR is the abbreviation for the former UK tax authority, the Inland Revenue
a few means some

explanation.surface: A handful of extremists have been taken on by the tax office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' looks political, but in chemistry a radical is a group of atoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry links them: an isomer is a compound with the same atoms rearranged, and a radical is a chemical group, so one stands loosely for the other.

clue.text: Girl with recipe having star quality

parts.note: Stella is a girl's name
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin 'recipe', take

explanation.surface: A young woman with her own cookery formula shines like a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar describes something starlike or outstanding, the quality of a star performer.

clue.text: Tomato and egg starters, some rice and ox I make, Japanese style

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of the words tomato and egg
only some of the word rice is used, its last two letters dropped

parts.note: a yak is a kind of ox

explanation.surface: A recipe list: tomato, egg, rice and beef cooked the Japanese way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Teriyaki is a Japanese cooking method of glazing meat with a sweet soy marinade.

clue.text: Sediment got with 80% of beer, say

indicators.note: four letters of a five-letter word is eighty per cent, so the closing four are kept

parts.note: beer is an example of booze, alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Dregs left behind once most of a pint has been drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first of five letters leaves the 80% that is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Ooze is soft mud or slime deposited on a sea or river bed, a kind of sediment.

clue.text: Behold! Carol is down

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold
to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: A Christmas scene: look, the singer is feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: A side that is down, behind in the score, is currently losing the game.

clue.text: Working in footballers' wives cars

indicators.note: the word in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: WAGs is the British press term for wives and girlfriends of footballers
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Footballers' partners with jobs, and the vehicles they drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway wagons are cars of a train, and wagons can also mean motor vehicles.

clue.text: Three little piggies — one's not English — in close proximity

indicators.note: one of the pieces loses E, the abbreviation for English

parts.note: 'this little piggy' is the nursery game played on toes, so three piggies are three toes

explanation.surface: A nursery rhyme with one foreign piggy, ending up squashed together.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of the three loses its E, leaving TO between the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: Toe to toe describes people standing face on, very near each other, as in a confrontation.

clue.text: Scandinavian myths collected by gifted Dane

indicators.note: the letters are gathered within the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Nordic legends gathered by a talented man from Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are Old Norse collections of poems and tales about the Norse gods and heroes.

clue.text: Me, I'm adult; I can surf all the different channels

indicators.note: surfing, flicking around, throws the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A grown-up boasting of the right to flick through every television station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surf' suggests channel-hopping in the surface, but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Multimedia combines several forms of communication, such as text, sound and video, at once.

clue.text: Pen for hairdresser with no schedule

indicators.note: says the second piece is removed from the first

parts.note: a stylist cuts and styles hair
a list is a schedule of items

explanation.surface: A writing implement for a barber who keeps no appointment book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool but is an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigpen is an enclosure for pigs, and a pen is any small animal enclosure.

clue.text: A jolly commercial set on a number of ships

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
an advertisement, ad, is a commercial

explanation.surface: A cheerful television advert set aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective, but is the nickname for a marine.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, a large group of vessels.

clue.text: Take the tops of red and green strips of cloth

indicators.note: the tops of words in a clue written across are their first letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for snipping the ends off coloured ribbons.
explanation.definitionFit: Rags are scraps of worn or torn fabric, old pieces of material.

clue.text: Consider standard class value

definitions.meaning: to consider something good is to judge or reckon it so
a fixed charge or a grade

explanation.surface: Weigh up the usual worth of a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Rate means to judge, and also a set price or level of quality, as in first-rate.

clue.text: See 2
Bell sound welcomes the weak doing work on the farm

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ting is the light ringing note of a bell
being ill makes one weak

explanation.surface: A village bell rings out for the frail as farmers toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilling is ploughing and preparing soil for crops, a basic farming job.

clue.text: Money gone (almost), determining how life started, some say

indicators.note: working out, settling the order of the letters afresh
almost the whole word, short of its final letter

explanation.surface: Cash nearly spent while working out the origin of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of gone, leaving GON to shuffle with MONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomogeny is the theory that life arose by natural law rather than by miracle, a view held by some.

clue.text: Girl's wrong to misrepresent

parts.note: Di is a girl's name; with the 's it gives DIS
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A young woman is mistaken and twists the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: To distort is to twist facts or give a false account of them.

clue.text: Route taken by boxer to the bout?

definitions.text: Route taken by boxer to the bout?

parts.words: Route taken by boxer to the bout?
parts.note: a boxer heads to the boxing ring, so his way there is jokingly a road to the ring; really a bypass around a town

explanation.surface: A fighter's journey to the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A town bypass circling a centre is named for its shape, which the boxing arena's name puns on.

clue.text: Hitch up, then come down; it happens early in the morning

definitions.text: it happens early in the morning

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to get hitched is to wed
to come down is to fall

explanation.surface: Marry, then crash, all before breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewfall is the forming of dew, moisture settling overnight and at dawn.

clue.text: Behold! The city church

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Look: a cathedral in the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecce is Latin for look or see, as in 'Ecce homo'.

clue.text: Contemporary officer takes Ms Herzigova in

indicators.note: takes in means holds inside, putting one piece within another
completes the phrase takes ... in, signalling one piece inside another

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
Eva Herzigova is a Czech supermodel

explanation.surface: A modern-day army commander escorts a famous model.
explanation.definitionFit: Coeval means of the same age or period, existing at the same time.

clue.text: Breakfast fare a number heard to consider first

indicators.note: the word for consider comes before the number
said aloud, the word for consider is written with its last two letters swapped

parts.note: to muse is to consider
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cereal for which a figure must be weighed up beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit.

clue.text: Temptress has split loyalties, yes? No!

indicators.note: split loyalties are broken up, their letters shuffled
says the letters of the word yes are not wanted and come out of the mix

explanation.surface: A seductress who serves two masters: will she agree? Never.
explanation.walkthrough: Take Y, E, S from the letters of loyalties and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita, from Nabokov's novel, is used for a sexually precocious young seductress.

clue.text: Individual comes into money

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A person inherits a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A single person or thing is a lone unit, a single one.

clue.text: Old writer playing in a doll's house?

definitions.text: Old writer playing in a doll's house?

parts.words: Old writer playing in a doll's house?
parts.note: the Norwegian dramatist wrote the play A Doll's House, so his name is 'playing' there

explanation.surface: An elderly author having fun with a child's toy home.
explanation.definitionFit: A nineteenth-century Norwegian playwright whose most famous drama is A Doll's House.

clue.text: Bitter when jungle fever affected all but Jack

indicators.note: the fever has affected the letters, upsetting their order
everything except, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for Jack in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Resentful after a tropical illness struck everyone except one man.
explanation.walkthrough: Without J the letters of jungle fever are ULNGLEFEVER to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bitter and resentful is set on getting their own back.

clue.text: Hears idea revealing alternate water source

indicators.note: every other letter is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a notion that uncovers another spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes, a huge body of fresh water.

clue.text: "Dam' right", Roseanne

parts.note: a bar is a barrier across water, like a dam

explanation.surface: A sitcom star's catchphrase with a mild curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam'' looks like a softened swear word but is a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseanne Barr is the American comedian and sitcom actress.

clue.text: It's grand in Liverpool once a year, of course!

definitions.text: It's grand in Liverpool once a year, of course!

parts.words: It's grand in Liverpool once a year, of course!
parts.note: the Grand ... is the annual steeplechase run at Aintree racecourse near Liverpool, so it is grand there on the course

explanation.surface: A cheerful claim that Liverpool is splendid annually, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand National is Britain's most famous horse race, held each spring at Aintree.

clue.text: Parent clumsily handled old medical tool

indicators.note: something handled clumsily is knocked about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mother or father fumbling with an antique surgical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A trepan was a surgeon's saw for cutting a hole in the skull.
